summary: A people can trace its descent to a common ancestor, as the two peoples descended from Rebekah do. Psalm 2 uses the plural beside “nations” for communities whose rulers gather against Yahweh.

senses.definition: Rebekah’s two sons will grow into two peoples, one stronger than the other. In the Psalms the peoples assemble, make plans and come under judgment as whole communities.

parallels.note: Each half of the verse names the nations or peoples whose plans come to nothing.

senses.definition: Genesis lists the Leummim beside the Asshurim and Letushim among the descendants of Dedan.

words.summary: The name has the plural form of the common noun. Genesis supplies the ancestry but does not explain the name.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 3007, art. لأم, form III, n43193

cognates.note: Gathering people offers a possible verbal comparison. The Arabic verb describes an action and does not establish the origin of the Hebrew noun.

note: TIPNR classifies Leummim as a group. The shared written plural gives the group key many common-noun matches. The particle בַּל, also returned for the common noun, is a separate word. Fisher p. 25 gives a Ugaritic comparison meaning people, but the consonantal spelling needs confirmation against the printed page.
